subject: Novatech POC: integration playbook & ownership (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Novatech POC: integration playbook & ownership (post-demo)

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Wanted to capture the call highlights, confirm success criteria you mentioned, and propose an initial integration playbook so we can lock timelines and owners. Below is the recap + concrete next steps.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: improve customer support triage accuracy for Novatech’s merchant disputes pipeline (reduce false positives, speed triage).
- Data: ~25k daily conversational events, typical request payloads include 2–6 short fields + customer messages. Average accepted latency target: sub-400ms p99 for single-request inference in the POC.
- Constraints: on-prem data retention for PII, required SOC2 evidence, and optional VPC deployment for production.

Proposed POC success criteria (draft — see attached spreadsheet for editable metrics)
1) Precision >= 78% on the triage label set (measured on your golden test set)
2) p95 latency <= 200ms and p99 <= 400ms for 1–2 concurrent requests in the target rig
3) End-to-end integration: SDK or streaming route accepts the live event and returns structured label + confidence within SLA
4) No PII persisted in hosted logs; audit log proof for any private deployment

Integration playbook (high level)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and sign technical MOU (we can use the HubSpot deal doc link).
- Week 1: Redwood provides SDK sample + API route mapping; Novatech provides sample event payloads and golden set (anonymized).
- Week 2: Onboard to staging account (dedicated trial model instance) and run smoke tests.
- Week 3: Run evaluation batch, track metrics in shared sheet, iterate prompt/config.
- Week 4: Acceptance demo and handoff to Novatech ops for production planning.

Ownership
- Redwood PM / AE: Marissa Cole (point for contract/acceptance)
- Redwood Tech lead: Ben Carter (integration, SDK walkthrough, on-call during POC)
- Redwood SRE: Soojin Lee (performance tuning, latency SLOs)
- Novatech POC lead: Emma Li (data & acceptance)
- Novatech Tech ops: Rajiv Patel (infrastructure, credentials)

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Wednesday?)
- Emma: confirm the three acceptance metrics above or suggest edits.
- Rajiv: share a sanitized sample payload + expected qps for POC.
- Ben/Soojin: please attach the SDK sample and API route mapping before EOD Tuesday.

Attachments: novatech_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (metrics + tracking), api-route-mapping.drawio (route map), novatech-sdk-sample.patch (small SDK diff).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar hold for a 30-min tech handshake once we confirm the sample payload.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — adding the technical detail we discussed on the call. Attaching a minimal SDK sample and a mapped list of API routes. Highlights below.

Quick technical notes
- Preferred integration: use our streaming socket for lower tail latency when you expect bursts; otherwise the single-request REST route /v1/generate is simplest to run in staging.
- For structured outputs we recommend function-style tool-calling (JSON schema enforcement). See sample in the SDK patch (function register + schema).
- KV cache: if you will reuse prefixes (customer history), enable prefix cache in config to reduce token cost. We'll provide a suggested cache TTL.

API route mapping (summary)
- /v1/generate (REST) — easiest for quick test harness (sync response, JSON label + confidence).
- /v1/stream (WebSocket) — lower p95 for live events, better for sub-200ms goals under light load.
- /v1/toolcall — when you want to call downstream enrichment (e.g., enrich transaction data) with guaranteed idempotency.

Performance knobs we’ll tune during POC
- Model variant selection (smaller quantized variant for latency testing, then compare quality)
- Batching policy: continuous batching at 10–30ms window or disabled for single-request latency testing
- Prefetch & KV caching for repeated contexts

Attached: api-route-mapping.drawio, novatech-sdk-sample.patch

Action for Novatech engineering
- Share sanitized sample payloads and expected rates (qps/burst).
- Point us to the test environment credentials method (API key vs temporary signed token).

I’ll be on the call Tuesday 09/16 for the SDK walkthrough — sending a calendar invite once Marissa confirms time.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Technical Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Notes / clarifications

- Latency: our infra team prefers the WebSocket streaming route for the POC to mimic production bursts.
- Data sharing: we will provide an anonymized golden set by Monday (we have to run it through our data pipeline).
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence request — can Redwood share the SOC2 control list and how logs are isolated in a private deployment?

Risk / constraints
- We have a procurement freeze in mid-October; ideally the POC must complete acceptance by Oct 8 to get any mid-cycle budget approved. Can we compress the timeline?

Next steps (we propose)
- Rajiv will send the sanitized sample payload and a small test harness (expects REST and WS) by EOD Friday.
- Redwood / Ben to provide a trimmed latency-focused model variant and recommended batching config by Monday morning.

Thanks — Emma
